workflow.text: Scope for this descriptive study (replaces the larger plan where they differ): (1) Counts: yearly counts of M>=5 with ComCat's preferred magnitude (one preferred magnitude per event; report the mix of magnitude types by decade), decade means, and counts at ONE common threshold equal to the largest decade Mc. Describe a change in counts only if the decade means show it; aftershocks are kept and the paper says so. (2) b-value: Aki-Utsu maximum likelihood with the bin correction (dM = 0.1); standard error by Shi & Bolt (1982): sigma_b = 2.30 b^2 sqrt(sum (M_i - mean M)^2 / (N (N-1))) - b/sqrt(N) is Aki's, label it so if reported; bootstrap 95% intervals. Mc per decade by maximum curvature (+0.2) and goodness-of-fit (90/95%), estimated from events down to M4.5. Pairwise decade comparisons by Utsu's test, reported exactly as computed (say which pairs overlap and which do not). (3) Checks: Mw-family-only sample and shallow (depth <= 70 km) sample. (4) Drop: ETAS/Poisson simulations, all three declustering methods, regional exclusions, 5-year and sliding windows, mb->Mw conversions, synthetic validation, LOESS, CUSUM/Pettitt. (5) Cite the catalogue as USGS ComCat (doi 10.5066/F7MS3QZH) for the data; cite only references that resolve in literature.bib; no JEL line. (6) A difference between the M>=5 and M>=5.5 counts is not a detection share; incompleteness below Mc lowers the estimated b, it does not raise it.

workflow.remark: Load ComCat from M>=4.5, not M>=4.0: Mc is about 5 in every decade, so events down to 4.5 are enough to estimate it, and M>=4.0 roughly doubles the load (worldwide M4 is far from complete and mostly regional-network ML/md events). Change the five load commands to --min-magnitude 4.5, rename eq_clean_m40 to eq_clean_m45 and drop the n_m40 column; keep everything else (no --event-type so the type counts exist, the ComCat citation, the GCMT 'unavailable' entry). In eq_bvalue_windows keep only the five decades (no sliding windows) and Mc rules maxc+0.2, gft90/95 and the common threshold (largest decade Mc); drop declustering from known_limits wording ('aftershocks are included and not removed').

workflow.remark: Three fixes in run_estimation.py, then run it so it writes estimation_results.json (no number typed by hand): (1) Counts must use the same threshold as the data table: eq_annual_counts.n_m50 counts mag >= 5.0 (83,469 events, decade means 1,595.9/1,617.4/1,390.6/1,992.8/1,750.2), but the script counts the 0.1-rounded magnitude (mi >= 50), i.e. mag >= 4.95 (83,543 events, mean 1,670.86). Count on the published magnitude (mag >= threshold, e.g. 5.0, 6.0, 7.0, and the common threshold) so the results match eq_annual_counts and the figure; keep the 0.1 binning only for Mc and b. (2) The Mw-family-only b at the common threshold 4.9 (b 0.51-0.80) is not a b-value of a complete sample: moment magnitudes are only assigned to larger events and that sample's own Mc is 5.2-5.6. Drop b_common_threshold and its pair tests for the Mw-only check; keep b at its own Mc. (3) Record that Mc = 4.5 (maxc, gft90, gft95 for 1996-2025) equals the load floor (M>=4.5): the estimate is censored there, Mc may be lower; add a field saying so. No other method change.

workflow.remark: Seven corrections, no new analysis: (1) Data section: 'published to one decimal' is false - 909 events carry two-decimal magnitudes (96 of them between 4.9 and 5.0). Say counts use the published magnitude and Mc/b use magnitudes binned to 0.1. (2) Counts at 4.9: delete the sentence attributing the difference to the M>=5 counts to events 'incompletely recorded in the first decades'. The extra events are simply those between 4.9 and 5.0, which the Gutenberg-Richter relation makes numerous, and our own Mc (max curvature +0.2) is at most 4.9 in every decade. Report the rank correlation 0.51 at 4.9 vs 0.27 at 5.0 without an explanation. (3) Pairwise tests at maxc+0.2: 'rejects equality for eight of ten pairs' is misleading. Write: the likelihood-ratio test rejects equality at the 1 percent level in nine of ten pairs; the exception is 2006-2015 vs 2016-2025 (2.4, p = 0.119); bootstrap intervals overlap for that pair and for 1976-1985 vs 2006-2015 (7.6, p = 0.006). Make the abstracts say 'nine of ten pairs'. (4) Common threshold: every decade uses the same threshold, not 'the same events'. (5) Delete 'the size of the differences, between 0.1 and 0.3, is small relative to the changes in magnitude-type composition' (b-units and type shares cannot be compared), and say 'all full-sample variants' (the Mw-only estimates for the two latest decades are 0.921 and 0.995). (6) Do not lean toward the magnitude-procedure reading: in Results drop 'consistent with the interpretation that the recent rise ... is tied to events between about 4.7 and 5.2', and in the Discussion drop 'which is what we observe'. The Mw-only sample has Mc 5.2-5.6 and far fewer events, so the contrast cannot separate a physical change from a catalogue change; state both as open. (7) Delete 'Each of these is a scope condition and not a flaw of the description: it bounds what the record can say.'
